claims.text: A baseline Heusler alloy can have a significant magnetocaloric effect while its phase-transition temperature is not optimally near room temperature.
The baseline Heusler alloy exhibits moderate hysteresis.
Adding a low concentration of an alloying element can fine-tune an alloy's behavior.
Co or a similar dopant is a suitable low-concentration addition for tuning the magnetocaloric behavior of a Heusler alloy.
Controlled processing can prevent phase inhomogeneities in the doped Heusler alloy.
The dopant adjusts the Heusler alloy's electronic structure.
The dopant adjusts phase stability in the Heusler alloy.
Dopant-induced changes in electronic structure and phase stability refine the balance between magnetic exchange interactions and structural transitions.
The refined balance between magnetic and structural interactions produces a sharper and more reversible magnetic phase transition.
A small dopant concentration alters local magnetic interactions and electron density.
Altered local magnetic interactions and electron density shift the phase-transition temperature closer to room temperature.
The dopant reduces kinetic barriers associated with the phase transition.
Shifting and refining the magnetic phase transition enhances the isothermal entropy change.
Reducing hysteresis minimizes energy losses.
The doped Heusler alloy will exhibit a stronger magnetocaloric effect near room temperature than the undoped alloy.
The doped alloy will have a larger isothermal entropy change than the undoped alloy.
The doped alloy will have less magnetic hysteresis than the undoped alloy.
Improvement requires preservation of the Heusler phase stability.
Dopant concentrations outside a narrow optimum may fail to shift the transition appropriately or may induce secondary phases that degrade the magnetocaloric effect.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing transition temperature, isothermal entropy change, and hysteresis between doped and undoped samples.
